metadata.title: AI Content vs. Human Creativity: What Works Better?
metadata.audience: Marketers, creators and students who run a brand's content across platforms
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Italian (one word). Hola/Namaste/Hej already used in this series. Chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI on every Claude page (B00, B03, B08, B09) and the outro.
metadata.note: ai-explainer, Plain register. New reel (not a variation): content repurposing — one human-made long-form video → clips, captions, blog, carousel, posts — and the AI-vs-human question answered task by task. NO statistics: every example (captions, voice guide, drafts) is labelled illustrative. Reel-local C3 scenes live in runtime/remotion/src/scenes/ContentRepurpose.tsx (+ ContentRepurpose916.tsx). Outro is HandleTitleOutro. Never publishes.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI first; the ask lands answered. Chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI.
beats.narration_text: Ciao. Everyone's asking the same question: A I content or human creativity, which works better? So I asked Claude what happens when you take one long video and let A I turn it into content for every platform.

show.event: composer fades in; greeting 'Ciao, Shubh'
the ask types into the composer
send arms; runningText 'mapping the assets…'
three result lines cascade

props.command: I made one long-form video. Can AI turn it into clips, captions, carousels, a blog and social posts — and still sound like my brand?
output: short clips + captions for every platform
a blog post, a carousel, social posts
one condition: a human keeps the voice

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer. Misconception: AI content BEATS (competes with) human creativity, and one video = one post → AI SCALES human creativity; one video makes a WEEK OF POSTS. Narration opens 'Hi, I'm Shubh… this video is about…' per the brief.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Shubh, and this video is about A I content versus human creativity, and why the real answer is both. A I can turn one long video into a week of posts across platforms. Human creativity makes sure every piece still sounds like you.

show.event: cream page; caret blinks
types 'AI content beats human creativity.'
'beats' turns terracotta, backspaces, becomes 'scales'
types 'One video makes a post.'
'post' turns terracotta, backspaces, becomes 'week of posts'
corrected overview settles

props.text:
AI content

creativity.

makes a

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the human original is the source; AI's job is finding moments, not inventing them. Timeline performs: chapters draw, terracotta playhead scans, three moment markers drop in spoken order.
beats.narration_text: Start with one strong piece made by a person: a long-form video. That's where the ideas, the stories and your voice already live. A I's job isn't to invent them. Its job is to find the best moments inside, like the hook, the story and the practical tip.

show.event: long timeline bar draws: 'Your long-form video — made by a person'
chapter blocks fill the bar: ideas, stories, your voice
terracotta playhead scans the timeline ('find the best moments')
markers drop in spoken order: Hook, Story, Tip

props.jobLine: AI finds the moments. It doesn’t invent them.

beats.role_note: ASK→RESULT micro-beat, mid-reel Claude page (chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI). Command pre-typed (inner beat). Output lines are the plan, not fabricated findings.
beats.narration_text: So I hand Claude the transcript and ask for the three best moments, each with a caption written in our brand voice.

show.event: composer with the ask already typed
runningText 'reading the transcript…'
three output lines: hook, story, tip

props.command: Here's the transcript of my video. Find the three strongest moments for short clips, and write a caption for each in our brand voice.

beats.role_note: RESULT of B03 — the three moments lift off the timeline into vertical phone frames with example captions; the human pick gets the one accent ring. Captions labelled as examples.
beats.narration_text: Those three moments become vertical clips for Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts, each with a caption and on-screen text. A I handles the trimming, the resizing and the first-draft captions. You still choose which cut actually lands.

show.event: compact timeline with three highlighted segments
each segment lifts into a vertical phone frame: Reels, TikTok, Shorts
an example caption appears under each clip
'You choose' — terracotta ring lands on one clip

props.aiLine: AI trims, resizes and drafts captions.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — the derivative chain performs in spoken order (video → transcript → blog → carousel → posts + newsletter); the accent trace runs back to the original on 'traces back'.
beats.narration_text: And it keeps cascading. The transcript becomes a blog post. The blog's key points become a carousel. Those slides become social posts and a newsletter. One recording, a whole week of content, and every piece traces back to the original.

show.event: 'Long-form video' node
Transcript node lights
Blog post node
Carousel node
Social posts + Newsletter nodes
terracotta trace runs from the last nodes back to the original

props.sparkLine: One recording, a week of content.

beats.role_note: Consistency / brand voice — an example voice guide; one draft line flags off-brand (accent), is struck through and rewritten on the spoken word.
beats.narration_text: Here's how you keep the brand voice. Give A I a short voice guide: how you sound, words you use, and words you never use. Every draft gets checked against it. When a line drifts off-brand, you catch it and rewrite it before it goes out.

show.event: voice guide card fills: Sound / Use / Never
draft post card appears beside it
off-brand line flagged (terracotta), struck through
rewritten line types in; 'on-brand' check

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — the title question answered task by task: markers slide toward AI or Human, side by side, held; verdict line + terracotta rule.
beats.narration_text: So, what works better? On speed, volume and formatting, A I wins easily. On the original idea, the story and the final call, people win. Content that's only A I tends to sound like everyone else. Content that's only human struggles to keep up. What works best is the pair.

show.event: two poles appear: AI · People
Speed, Volume, Formatting markers slide to AI
Original idea, Story, Final call markers slide to People
verdict 'AI for scale. People for meaning.' + terracotta rule

beats.role_note: Verdict artifact page (Claude UI is the subject). Chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI via brandLabel.
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Start with one human-made original. Let A I find the moments, cut the clips and draft the captions, carousels, blogs and posts. Keep a voice guide, and keep a person on the final call.

show.event: artifact card opens
five lines stagger in, the rule last

artifactLines: A person makes the final call.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed. Chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Here's the transcript of my latest video and three lines about how my brand sounds. Turn it into three short clips with captions, one carousel and one LinkedIn post, and flag any line that doesn't sound like me. That last part is the point. It makes Claude check its own drafts against your voice, so you can see exactly where your judgment is needed.

show.event: greeting 'Your turn.'; the suggested prompt types in
runningText 'paste this into Claude…'

props.command: Here's the transcript of my latest video and three lines about how my brand sounds. Turn it into three short clips with captions, one carousel and one LinkedIn post, and flag any line that doesn't sound like me.

beats.role_note: OUTRO LAW — title restate, terracotta punctuation, handle @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI, HAI mark full-size.
beats.narration_text: A I content versus human creativity. What works better? Both, together. At Shubh, and at Humanitarians A I.

show.event: spark + title restated, terracotta question mark
handle '@Shubh & @HumanitariansAI' + HAI wordmark
